thread.title: Here's why investors should be hanging onto a battered Amazon right now

author: morningstar.com
title: Here's why investors should be hanging onto a battered Amazon right now
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
Snow and the worst start to the quarter since 1929 -- so much for Wall Street's April kickoff.
(https://twitter.com/PeterHoskinsTV/status/980866028086456322)
In the fallout from yesterday's tech exodus, the S&P slipped under its 200-day moving average (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-selloff-threatens-lengthy-stretch-above-key-technical-level-2018-04-02) -- a key gauge of long-term momentum -- and the Dow transports tumbled into "sell" signal- land (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-transports-tumble-into-dow-theory-sell-signal-territory-2018-04-02) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-transports-tumble-into-dow-theory-sell-signal-territory-2018-04-02). All of which is likely to keep investors on edge today.
(https://twitter.com/TruthGundlach/status/980966803089195008)
That jittery state is right where they belong, says the always-entertaining Dr. Fly of the iBankCoin (http://ibankcoin.com/flyblog/2018/04/02/futures-yellen-soft-come-get-exodus-baboon-titted-manlet/) blog: "The Trumptarded market can't stop tripping over itself and is bound to have a fantastical conclusion. If it trades up tomorrow, fade it. If it gaps down lower -- get in on the momentum train lower and short ... stocks -- because margin calls are just around the bend."
But a different sort of battle cry is heard in our call of the day, which urges investors to stick with one of the big, battered technology stocks at the heart of recent market mayhem.
"We expect more chatter out of the White House on Amazon throughout Trump's time in office," PiperJaffray analysts Michael Olson and Sam Kemp said in a note to clients. "We, however, believe that little will change which has the potential to negatively impact Amazon's growth trajectory."
To recap, Amazon (AMZN) has been getting battered since POTUS last week declared a fairly public war (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/its-war-trump-reportedly-seeking-ways-to-hurt-amazon-2018-04-02) on the e-commerce seller, accusing it of cheating the Post Office, for one.
Olson and Kemp say if the Post Office decides to raise rates on Amazon, Bezos and the gang could take their business elsewhere. And even if customers end up having to pay higher sales taxes, they still won't lose their fiercely loyal shoppers (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-may-have-a-beef-with-amazon-but-consumers-cant-get-enough-of-it-2018-03-30).
It comes down to this, say the Piper analysts, pointing to a survey they conducted of 2,000 U.S. Amazon customers: It shows just 5% view sales tax as a big factor when deciding where to shop.
"In other words, even if there are changes to how Amazon collects sales tax in the U.S., our survey points to a very small impact on the core retail business," say the analysts
They have an overweight rating on Amazon and a $1,650 price target -- and that means the current level of $1,371.99 may be a bit of a bargain.
Opinion:Using antitrust laws to break up Amazon, Facebook and Google is just political fantasy (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/using-antitrust-laws-to-break-up-amazon-facebook-and-google-is-just-political-fantasy-2018-04-03)
Key market gauges
Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures are creeping up, led by tech. That sector is also taking a hit in Europe, where markets are slumping after a long weekend break (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-slump-as-techs-follow-us-lead-lower-2018-04-03). Asia had a largely down day, also led by techs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tech-shares-pull-down-asian-markets-2018-04-02).
Gold and the dollar (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-weakens-to-kick-off-april-2nd-quarter-after-woeful-start-to-2018-2018-04-02)are both off a bit, while crude is up about 0.5%.
See the Market Snapshot column (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stocks-poised-for-a-higher-but-nervous-start-after-tech-driven-selloff-2018-04-03) for the latest action.
The chart
If markets are locked into a bout of high volatility, it can last for about five to six weeks. But if you're waiting for the S&P 500 to bottom, then you're looking at a wait of about twice that. That's according to this chart from Deutsche Bank, as noted by The Daily Shot (https://blogs.wsj.com/dailyshot/2018/04/03/the-daily-shot-are-markets-anticipating-the-end-of-current-economic-cycle/).
The buzz
If Apple (AAPL) delivers on making its own chips to power Mac computers, that could lift its earnings per share by 25 to 25 cents, say analysts at RBC Capital in a note. Intel (INTC) sank 6% yesterday after Bloomberg reported (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/intel-amazon-and-tesla-lead-tech-stocks-lower-on-the-first-trading-day-of-april-2018-04-02) that Apple plans to replace its processors within two years. Separately, KeyBanc sees Intel taking a 21 to 28-cent hit on EPS if it loses the Mac maker as a customer.
As for troubled Tesla (TSLA) , CEO Elon Musk has confirmed (https://twitter.com/elonmusk/status/980910671763193856) a news report that he's taking charge of Model 3 production (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/elon-musk-takes-over-production-for-teslas-model-3-report-2018-04-03) -- and it looks like he'll be bedding down on the factory floor again to do it.
Walmart (WMT) reportedly wants to buy online pharmacy startup PillPack, (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/walmart-in-talks-to-buy-online-pharmacy-pillpack-report-2018-04-02) days after it was reported to be in early talks to buy Humana (HUM) .
Fox (FOX) is wooing U.K. regulators into approving its Sky (SKY.LN) buy with a new proposal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/disney-could-buy-sky-news-fox-tells-uk-watchdog-2018-04-03): It'll separate off Sky News, or maybe sell it to Disney (DIS) .
Sinclair (SBGI) has gone on the defense over media-bashing (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sinclair-broadcast-defends-itself-after-backlash-over-scripted-fake-news-promos-2018-04-02) promos.
Who would win a U.S.-China trade war? It's more likely to be what, rather than who, says Ken Rogoff (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/whos-going-to-win-chinese-workers-or-robots-2018-04-02).
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/white-house-investigates-epa-chief-pruitt-over-sweet-rental-deal-2018-04-02)No major data reports today, but updates on auto sales should trickle out -- though GM says it will abandon monthly figures (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gm-abandons-monthly-sales-reports-2018-04-03).
Check out: MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
And:Get ready for slower hiring likely in March (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/crazy-fast-pace-of-new-job-creation-cant-last-can-it-slower-hiring-likely-in-march-2018-04-01)
The stat
Analysts are way upbeat about the coming earnings season, which kicks off next week.
For the first-quarter 2018 reporting period, which is just around the corner, the estimated earnings growth rate for the S&P 500 is 17.3%. That would mark the highest growth since the first quarter of 2011, when it came in at 19.5%, says FactSet senior earnings analyst John Butters.
Random reads
Villanova are the NCAA men's basketball champs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/villanova-rolls-past-michigan-to-win-second-ncaa-tournament-in-three-years-2018-04-02)
Migrant "caravan"? Here's what's pushing POTUS's button (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/when-trump-mentions-migrant-caravan-this-is-what-hes-talking-about-2018-04-02)
Uncongratulations to world's most unequal country (https://www.npr.org/sections/goatsandsoda/2018/04/02/598864666/the-country-with-the-worlds-worst-inequality-is).
Stephen Hawking had one last parting gift (https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/stephen-hawkings-incredible-final-gift-12294400) for his hometown of Cambridge.
The White House is investigating EPA chief Scott Pruitt over reports he rented cheap housing from an energy lobbyist. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/white-house-investigates-epa-chief-pruitt-over-sweet-rental-deal-2018-04-02)
